newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse heads higher, but nerves jangling.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse heads higher, but nerves jangling.

text.p: The booming Brussels bourse set new record highs on Wednesday as strong sentiment, low interest rates and Belgian pharmaceutical firm UCB overran a spate of dividend payments, but traders warned of fraying nerves.
"This is not a market to go short in, but nevertheless we are starting to see profittaking coming out," one trader said.
"Day after day records are being broken. New issues are being snapped up as buyers look for something to buy. The markets are feeding on themselves," another trader said.
"Who knows if it will continue. It could be hit by adverse developments either in the United States or Europe," he added.
"If the European Union's summit in Amsterdam next week is a disaster, interest rates will go up, uncertainty will increase and the bourse will go down," the trader said.
"But at the moment even if you go to a client and say you think this market is too expensive, they will listen to all your arguments and then buy it anyway," he added.

The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares climbed 0.45 percent to set a new closing record high of 2,362.70 after earlier setting a new intra-day high of 2,371.02. Just under five billion francs of shares were traded.
The index had been expected to drop between 16 and 17 points gross with five issues going ex-dividend.
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, insurer Fortis AG, insurer Royale Belge, utility holding firm Tractebel and chemical firm Solvay all paid dividends on Wednesday.
All lost ground heavily to start with but then, to varying degrees, clawed back some of their losses.
Conversely issues such as non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere and Kredietbank, recent strong performers, suffered mild profittaking losses.
But it was UCB that was the star of the day, jumping 10.9 percent or 11,050 francs to 111,850 after earlier leaping 13 percent to 114,000 francs.

Traders said the remarkable leap was due to a combination of strongly positive remarks at Tuesday's annual meeting, the possibility of a share split and the fact the share had finally broken up through the stiff psychological barrier of 100,000 francs.
